idiom_name: test class implements the outgoing interface and passes this (lambda/anonymous class for one-method seams)
implementation_notes: Java test classes are ordinary classes, so the canonical form is a JUnit class that implements the collaborator interface and passes this to the SUT; this is the form in Meszaros' example and needs no framework. Since Java 8, an interface with one abstract method can instead be implemented by a lambda or anonymous class declared inside the test method, capturing fixture fields, which confines the double to one test (an Inner Test Double) and is the lighter option for a single callback. Use the whole-class shunt when several tests in the case share the callback, and Mockito (mock/spy/verify) once programmed expectations or call-count verification replace simple recording.
pitfalls: Single inheritance bounds the shunt: a test class that must extend a legacy TestCase or a Spring test base class can only add the interface, so any other helper type has to be composed rather than extended.
Multi-method interfaces must be implemented in full unless they carry default methods, and placeholder bodies fail far from the cause when the SUT calls one.

A callback method whose name or signature collides with framework lifecycle (setUp, tearDown, a no-arg method matching test discovery) can be run or skipped unexpectedly; keep interface methods distinct from hook names.
